problem.claim: Train models when objectives are evaluated by sampling, particularly with terminal binary feedback that induces likelihood over correct rollouts.

gap.claim: Expected-reward RL is described as only a first-order approximation to the induced likelihood, despite maximum likelihood being the natural framework.

contributions.claim: Introduces MaxRL, a compute-indexed family of sample-based objectives interpolating between expected-reward RL and maximum likelihood as sampling compute increases.
Provides an objective requiring a one-line change to standard RL implementations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MaxRL as a compute-indexed bridge between expected-reward RL and maximum likelihood for this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MaxRL Pareto-dominates existing methods across all tested models and tasks.
The authors report up to 20× higher test-time scaling efficiency than GRPO.
The authors report more favorable scaling with additional training data and compute.

narrative_sequence.summary: RL is positioned as the standard choice when objectives are accessible only through model sampling.
Terminal binary feedback is said to induce a likelihood over correct rollouts, making maximum likelihood a natural formulation.
The standard expected-reward RL objective is proved to be a first-order likelihood approximation.
MaxRL is introduced to interpolate between RL and maximum likelihood with increased sampling compute, using a one-line implementation change.
The authors report broad tested-task dominance, up to 20× test-time scaling-efficiency gains over GRPO, and improved scaling with data and compute.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a feedback structure—terminal and binary—to an induced likelihood, then aligns the proposed objective with that structure.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research move is to derive the optimization target from the statistical structure of the feedback before selecting a workaround.
lessons.application: For another sampled-feedback problem, explicitly identify whether feedback induces a tractable likelihood and design an objective that approaches it under a controllable compute parameter.
lessons.exception: This move may not apply when feedback is nonterminal, nonbinary, or does not define a meaningful likelihood.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the tested models, tasks, baselines beyond GRPO, or conditions underlying the reported Pareto dominance and 20× maximum.

The abstract identifies terminal binary feedback and describes interpolation from expected-reward RL toward maximum likelihood as sampling compute increases, but does not give the precise objective formula or full proof assumptions.
